title: Legacy serialized scorers must reload with timeout=0, not the fresh-scorer default
answers: why did my existing registered scorer start timing out after upgrade
what timeout do scorers loaded from old JSON get
how is the scorer timeout serialized
why does a deserialized scorer have timeout 0
body:
Symptom: scorers registered before the timeout feature suddenly get bounded at 300 s in online monitoring after upgrading.
Root cause: the timeout field default must differ by path. Scorer.timeout defaults to None (meaning DEFAULT_SCORER_TIMEOUT), but SerializedScorer.timeout defaults to 0, so a payload without the key reloads unbounded.
Fix pattern: keep SerializedScorer.timeout defaulted to 0 and pass serialized.timeout through in _reconstruct_decorator_scorer. Fresh scorers serialize their None value through Scorer.model_dump.
Constraints: changing SerializedScorer's default to None would silently bound every legacy scorer. Covered by test_scorer_serialized_before_timeout_existed_deserializes_to_zero in tests/genai/scorers/test_serialization.py.
applies: Changes to SerializedScorer, Scorer.model_dump, or decorator-scorer reconstruction in mlflow/genai/scorers/base.py.
says: Registered model scorers suddenly time out during online monitoring after system upgrades.
Existing evaluation metrics stop running and fail after five minutes in production.
Previously saved custom scorers should continue running without unexpected timeout limits.
Upgraded model monitoring triggers false timeout errors on legacy evaluation metrics.
Prevent system upgrades from imposing default timeout limits on existing registered scorers.
search: Deserialized legacy scorers must reload with timeout=0 to remain unbounded rather than adopting the default assigned to fresh scorers. In mlflow/genai/scorers/base.py, Scorer.timeout defaults to None (DEFAULT_SCORER_TIMEOUT), but SerializedScorer.timeout defaults to 0 and passes through _reconstruct_decorator_scorer so older payloads do not get capped at 300 seconds. Setting SerializedScorer's default to None would silently bound legacy scorers, as verified in tests/genai/scorers/test_serialization.py:test_scorer_serialized_before_timeout_existed_deserializes_to_zero.
